newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks leap to close at all time high.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks leap to close at all time high.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks leaped to an all-time high and record close on Wednesday, overcoming earlier weakness on futures-related activity and buying in favoured property developers, brokers said.

The Hang Seng index rose 45.62 points to end at 13,530.95, its highest level ever, off an early afternoon low of 13,347.62 and topping the previous record of 13,495.38 set on Tuesday. "We saw the start of a correction in the morning, but futures-related buying in the last hour of afternoon trading pushed the index up," said Jason Tang in institutional sales at South China Securities.

Turnover soared to HK$13.42 billion, boosted by a placement of 310 million shares by Amoy Properties. Amoy shares closed down HK$0.30 at HK$11.20, just above the placement price of HK$11.10, on total turnover of HK$3.57 billion.
Trading in Hang Seng Index futures was active with a total of 32,842 contracts traded. The November contract finished 95 points up at 13,640 and December put on 85 points to 13,675.
The November contract expires tomorrow and brokers noted the contract has traded at a slight premium to the market for most of the month.
Many brokers remain cautiously optimistic on the market at this level.
"It is dangerous to sell this market at this time of year," said Angus Shillington, referring to the market's usual buoyant end-year, pre-Chinese New Year rally.
The utility sector led the market, followed by properties. Hongkong Telecom gained HK$0.10 to HK$13.20, Hongkong Electric put on HK$0.20 to HK$25.10 and China Light HK$0.10 to HK$33.20.
In the property sector Sun Hung Kai rose HK$1.50 to a new all time of HK$98.00. Henderson Land touched an all-time high of HK$79.50, then eased to close up HK$1.00 at HK$79.25.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings rose HK$0.50 to 163.50.
H shares, which rose against the trend in the morning, ended the day slightly down. Shanghai Petrochemial slid HK$0.025 to HK$2.00, and Tsingtao Brewery lost HK$0.075 to HK$2.60.
